hook_text: In 1969, two people walked on the Moon. How did they get there, and who has been to space since?
clip_script: 1957: a tiny satellite goes beep, beep, beep around the Earth. 1961: Yuri Gagarin, the first person in space. 1969: a giant rocket blasts off, and three days later, Neil Armstrong steps onto the Moon. One small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind. Twelve people have walked on the Moon. And in 2002, Mark Shuttleworth became the first South African in space. Rockets made it all possible.
visual_style: Whiteboard timeline from a beeping satellite, to a single astronaut circling the Earth, to a tall rocket launching three astronauts, to two astronauts planting footprints on the Moon, to a space station circling the Earth.
mood: Exciting and proud, like watching a big launch countdown.
pacing: A short timeline from the first satellite, to the first person in space, to the Moon landings, to space travel today.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look up when the space station will pass over your town.
